atoms.sound: The Scottish Highlands are the north-west region of the country. The area is coined by impressive green mountain ranges and widespread treeless moors. The Highlands are rather scarcely populated: With eight inhabitants per square kilometre they have the lowest population density in Scotland. Places of interest are for example Glenfinnan, a hamlet in front of a magnificent landscape, the Glenfinnan viaduct, a beautiful railroad in the countryside, the Inverness castle among many other charming castles, and numerous lochs, including Loch Ness.

• cityscape reflects Victorian and Art Nouveau ((++architecture construction)) of this period

atoms.sound: The harbour city of Glasgow is located in the Lowlands on the River Clyde and counts about 636,000 inhabitants. From the 18th to the 20th century, the city was an important trading and shipbuilding centre. The cityscape reflects the Victorian and Art Nouveau architecture of this period. Today, Glasgow is an important cultural centre with many museums, operas, theatres and ballets. Its thriving music scene and the many shopping centres are also attractive for visitors.

atoms.sound: The Argail and Bute Council Area offers picturesque landscapes. Besides the lovely little villages and towns you can explore impressive glens and Lochs. Although Loch gilpad is the capital, the biggest city of the region is Oban with 8,500 inhabitants. The Isle of Mull and the peninsula Kintyre are famous for fishing villages, their unique wildlife and biodiversity. In Argail, you can also hike parts of the Grampian Mountains which stretch across half of Scotland.
